interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index keeps advertising a log it no longer holds, fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader re-ships the same snapshot; the starvation persists while the newest snapshot index stays at or below the cached claim, ends once a snapshot above it is published, and reproduces at three and five voters and over a ten-second window. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977, tail at 1952-1977); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); prev-log verification then misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader walks nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps any suffix above the snapshot index while the monotonic branch deletes the whole store without resetting the claim (src_compaction, snapshot.go 217-279). Decided evidence: the settled comparison set (execution b6089b103bbb467199d051f4492e82c8, trimmed probe index 14) with the untrimmed control negative on the same fields (index 29); the monotonic-store variant, where the store was emptied while the claim persisted (execution 20c7c72772474093bd6093a37b84448f, probe index 14); the repair boundary, where driving the leader past the claim of 97 and publishing a snapshot at 98 restored the follower to the frontier (same receipt, probe index 33); the five-voter repetition, where the premise recorded a claim at index 102 in term 2 over a snapshot at 83 in term 3 and the probe again held on all three predicates (execution 14e86faf6ccc4b13af3ee46c65cc08dc, setup index 0 and probe index 14); and the ten-second persistence run, where the follower stayed at 83 while the frontier advanced to 123 with restores 5 -> 4883, the claim still (95, term 2) and one stable leader set (execution 8a3c426eb9094b3f9bd3cfb1004039be, setup index 0 and probe index 42). Counterevidence kept: the untrimmed control repairs the same history with entries alone, so the install path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger; a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so it never campaigns and the state is stable rather than self-healing; and the refusal is bounded by the claim, as the repair probe shows. Limits: store and snapshot implementations are the in-process ones (InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, its monotonic wrapper) with TrailingLogs=10 against a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250 ms sample, windows of 3-4 s and 10 s, voter counts of three and five, and one induced partition per case; a production BoltDB-style store is not available in the captured package, longer horizons are unmeasured, the follower's commit index staying 0 through the install path is reported as an advertised-state inconsistency rather than an independent defect, and the vote and configuration-change consequences of the same claim are decided separately in the child question with their own receipts.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with entries and reached the frontier in every run, and the ten-second window shows the trimmed case not resolving on its own.

The repair boundary (claim 97, snapshot 98, follower restored to the frontier) bounds the defect to the interval in which the leader's newest snapshot index remains at or below the follower's cached claim.
The monotonic-store case stalls with an empty log store, so a surviving on-disk suffix is not required; the operative state is the cached claim.
limitations: Store and snapshot implementations are the in-process ones; a production BoltDB-style store is not available in the captured package.
Windows measured are 3-4 s and 10 s with one write per sample, so frontier advance is bounded by that write rate; longer horizons are unmeasured.

The vote-decision and configuration-change consequences are decided in the child question and not re-measured here; the child's minority bound assumes no configuration change between the orphaned suffix and the snapshot install.
